title: Fusion Energy Race Update — Sun Jun 7, 2026
summary: A landmark week caps with mainstream media recognition of commercial fusion as near-term infrastructure: Scientific American and Hackaday featured CFS's PJM grid application on June 7 as the first fusion company ever to enter a U.S. wholesale electricity market queue. Helion Energy closed a $465M Series G at a $15.5B valuation (June 4), tripling its January 2025 value — funds go toward Orion, its Malaga, WA commercial power plant targeting 50 MW delivery to Microsoft by 2028. CFS published five peer-reviewed ARC physics papers (Journal of Plasma Physics) co-authored by 58 scientists confirming 400 MW net electricity from the commercial plant. Pacific Fusion's 440 GW pulser prototype (June 2) unlocked the next tranche of its $1B+ Series A, with demo facility construction starting this summer. New map points added for Pacific Fusion (Fremont, CA), Helion Orion (Malaga, WA), Focused Energy (Biblis, Germany), and Thea Energy (Princeton, NJ). Global private fusion investment now exceeds $10.6 billion.

title: Fusion Energy Race Update — May 28, 2026
summary: The U.S. NRC closed its 90-day public comment period on a proposed fusion-specific regulatory framework (Part 30 byproduct classification) around May 27, 2026, with a final rule targeted for fall 2026 — clearing a major commercial licensing barrier for companies like CFS, which already has a PJM grid application filed. Oxford-based First Light Fusion completed a £25M first-close funding round on April 21, with UKAEA as a strategic investor, to accelerate its FLARE inertial fusion concept. The fusion-2030s-grid-timeline claim was updated to reflect the NRC regulatory progress. ITER remains on its Baseline 2024 schedule, and JT-60SA continues integrated commissioning ahead of plasma experiments in late 2026.

title: Fusion Energy Race Update — May 21, 2026
summary: JT-60SA — the world's largest operational superconducting tokamak — completed major upgrades (new first wall, in-vessel coils, heating systems) and began integrated commissioning on May 15 under new project leader Jerónimo García, with plasma experiments planned for late 2026. On May 14, TAE Technologies and UKAEA formally launched TAE Beam UK, a joint venture at Culham Campus commercializing neutral beam and accelerator technology for food safety, cancer therapy, and homeland security — backed by a £5.6M UKAEA investment. China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026–2030) designates fusion as one of eight national frontier technology priorities backed by $6.5B+ since 2023. Jefferson Lab's $29M DOE spin-polarized fusion fuel project was spotlighted, with researchers targeting up to 80% yield efficiency gain for D-T reactions.

title: Fusion Energy Race Update — May 13, 2026

title: Fusion Energy Race Update — May 06, 2026
summary: China's EAST tokamak published a Physical Review Letters paper demonstrating the novel DTP (Detached divertor and Turbulence-dominated Pedestal) plasma regime on April 29 — the first in a metal-wall device — simultaneously achieving ELM-free high-confinement mode and divertor detachment for one minute, addressing a critical heat-load engineering challenge. The same day, Zap Energy appointed Zabrina Johal as CEO and announced a dual fission-fusion strategy adding 50 MW SMRs for near-term revenue amid softening private fusion investment rates. On May 4, a DOE-funded Savannah River National Laboratory study published in Fusion Science and Technology independently validated General Fusion's liquid metal wall design, finding it requires less start-up tritium and achieves shorter tritium doubling times than conventional tokamaks.
